texts.facts: In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 01.07.2018 police officials reached on intimation received at the spot of alleged accident. Later on during investigation, injured/petitioner was found unfit for statement. Further, one Chandan found in hospital who stated that he is an eye witness to the accident in question. Such Chandan stated that he alongwith Irfan and Jabbar were going on motorcycle bearing no. DL-3SCU-8646 Hero Honda Passion Pro at about 3.30 AM at night from Harkesh Nagar, Okhla Phase-2 to Govindpuri to bring food. When they were coming back, the petitioner/injured Jabbar was riding the motorcycle and thereafter Irfan was sitting and in the last such Chandan was sitting. At the place of accident, the offending vehicle/Truck bearing no. HR-69B0120 came from behind and hit them and starting running away from there but such Chandan caught him and called 100 number. Thereafter, PCR came and MACT No. 929/18 Jabbar Alam (DAR) v. Harbans Singh Page No. 2 of 29 BK took Jabbar to Trauma center, AIIMS. As such, FIR in question u/s 279/337 IPC was initially registered. Further, during investigation victim Jabbar also gave his statement, as per the IO, same is on the lines of original statement given by Chandan. Later on, after investigation chargesheet u/ s 279 and 338 IPC filed against R-1 as injuries were found grievous in nature as per MLC. 3. Further, Medical Board of Pt. Madan Mohan Hospital, Malviya Nagar, New Delhi sent disability report dated 30.04.2019 noticing 80% permanent physical impairment in relation to his left lower limb with amputation. 4. Further, as per record, R-1 and R-2 appeared, but they did not file any reply. 5. But reply filed by insurance company/R-3. In nutshell, in such reply, it is stated that the injured/petitioner suffered injuries due to his own negligence and he is responsible solely for the accident in question. It is further stated that it was the petitioner Jabbar Alam who was riding the motorcycle in question, although he is taking a false and contrary stand in the present case. It is further stated that petitioner was a minor at the time of accident and as such, he was driving such motorcycle in violation of MV Act. It is further stated that it is the case of triple riding and because of imbalance and negligence, petitioner himself, the accident in question took place. Thus, it is further submitted that at least there is contributory negligence on the part of petitioner himself. It is further claimed that as per verification report, registration of offending vehicle was valid upto MACT No. 929/18 Jabbar Alam (DAR) v. Harbans Singh Page No. 3 of 29 BK 01.08.2017 whereas accident took place on 01.07.2018. As such, it is stated that RC of the offending vehicle was not valid at the time of accident. Accordingly, it is claimed that insurance company is not liable to make any payment and there is violation of policy terms. 6. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed on 05.11.2018 by Predecessor of this Tribunal: Mohd. Jabbar Alam @ Jabbar@Mohd. Such PW-1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents including the discharge summary and medical bills, Estimate of artificial limb cost Ex. PW-1/1 (colly) till Ex. PW-1/6. He was cross- examined by learned counsel for insurance company/R-3. 8. PW-1 was cross-examined by learned counsel for R- 1/driver as well as by R-3/insurance company. 9. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. He further MACT No. 929/18 Jabbar Alam (DAR) v. Harbans Singh Page No. 4 of 29 BK relied upon document Ex. R-1W-1/1, his Aadhar card.
